Figure 112. Who held NYC taxi medallion loans, and where they moved, 2000 to 2025

Fixed nodes = lender families. Node area = medallions held at year end. Arrow width = medallions moved; in Memory (the default) recent moves are bold and older ones fade.

Time

Smooth: moves appear in the month they were filed; widths are the last 12 months. Self-loops and Markov shares stay calendar-year. Lapse exits appear at their mechanical 5-year lapse date, not when the loan was repaid.

Layout

Flow (default): lenders that trade heavily sit close together, so big moves are short arrows; position shows trading relationships, not lender type (node colour shows type). Hub: Public in the centre, lenders in arcs by type, ordered to keep big flows short and uncrossed. Columns: lender types side by side.

Colour nodes by

Days able to operate = days the medallion was on the TLC Authorized list. Not driving or hours. 2013 onward. Medallions were not randomly assigned to lenders (Figures 99, 107), so this describes, it does not prove a lender effect.

Medallions

No dollar amounts. Every number is a count of medallions (fractional where a loan is shared), not loan dollars. UCC filings record no loan principal.

Width
Window

.5123571015 2 yr

Moving dots travel in the direction of the move; more dots = more medallions. Only this year's moves carry dots, so faded older moves sit still.

Kinds
  • Sale (assigned): the loan is assigned to a new holder.
  • Refinanced: the borrower took a new loan from another lender within a year.
  • New loan: a medallion with no open lien (Public) gets a loan.
  • Exit: the lien is terminated or lapses; the medallion goes back to Public.
  • Merger or co-loan closed: the lender merged into another (Progressive into PenFed, Montauk into Bethpage), or one lender's share of a shared loan closed.
≥ 10

Hides arrows that move fewer than this many medallions, in both width modes, so the big moves stand out. Hidden flows still count in the inspector and in holdings.

Default 10: about 34 arrows a year carrying 90% of moved medallions (key network); 43 arrows, 69% (all lenders).

2000 to 2001: the filing record is thin (Figure 88); new-loan counts understate lending.

Events

Large type = major events: the sales of 250+ medallions (Capital One, Signature, Melrose and LOMTO to DePalma), the Melrose and LOMTO wind-up, Doral (the first lender failure), and the market turning points (Uber, price peak, COVID, MRP closings). Everything else is minor, in small type beneath. Each event is named on the strip and coloured by layer. Hover or click a lender on the map to highlight its events (the rest dim); click an event to jump to its year. "Book turns bad" (off by default) is each lender's first sign of trouble in its own filings (stage 232).

    Who counts as a key lender

    Size keys

    Read with care

    • No dollar amounts. Every number is a count of medallions (fractional where a loan is shared), not loan dollars. UCC filings record no loan principal.
    • Holder of record: a sale is dated by its assignment filing.
    • A sale can go unfiled, so some moves are missing or late.
    • Exits are mostly lapses, dated up to 5 years after payoff.
    • Public (no lender) = a medallion with no open UCC loan on record at that year end: not yet financed, loan terminated (released), loan lapsed (5-year UCC expiry, the largest share), or between loans. It is a state, not a group of people; lenders + Public = 13,122 medallions every year. Medallions never named by any UCC filing (~600) are outside the data. Not proof the owner is debt-free.
    • Colour by days able to operate: share of held days on the TLC Authorized list (stage 213a, 2013 onward; holders by all open loans, so its holder-years differ from the drawn stocks), relative to Public that year; cells under 30 medallion-years shown as no data. Days on the list, not driving or hours; lenders' books were not randomly assigned (Figures 99, 107).
    • Independent / Fleet split: each medallion's type is fixed at its spine value (1,330 drifted toward owner-must-drive count under their spine value); moves among small lenders inside Other lenders are not split by type.
    • Concentration strip: shares of lender-held medallions by lender family (each medallion once, under its latest loan); not comparable with Figure 82's HHI, which counts loans.
    • Moves among the small lenders inside "Other lenders" are drawn as a dotted self-loop on that node ("N moved among small lenders"); they are not arrows to named lenders.
    • 2000 to 2001: the filing record is thin (Figure 88), so new-loan counts understate lending in those years.
    • Dashed exit arrows = lien lapsed (dated 5 years after the last filing, not when the loan ended); solid = a filed termination.
    • Persistence = share of the start-of-year book still with the same holder at year end; moves within "Other lenders" count as staying.
    • Self-loop: arrow from a holder back to itself; width = the share (Markov share) or number (Medallions moved) of its start-of-year book that stayed, on the same scale as the outgoing arrows.
    • Self-loops stay year-specific in every window, including Memory and Since 2000.
    • Memory: each year's moves count half as much after every half-life (default 2 years), so recent moves are drawn strongest.
    • Memory colour strength = recency of the edge's last big year (a year carrying at least 20% of its largest single-year flow); it halves every 1.5 years after that year, at any half-life.
    • Memory share = decayed moves ÷ the sender's decayed start-of-year books (same half-life).
    • Timeline dates come from the project registries (_timeline.py, stages 229 and 232); stage 232 wins where they differ. MRP dates and the 2023 PenFed re-filing are from the project timeline notes.
    • Markov share = medallions moved ÷ sender's book at the start of the year.
    • Market share denominator = medallions held by any lender at the start of the year; Public excluded. Smooth: trailing 12 months ÷ lender-held medallions 12 months earlier. Self-loops in Market share = medallions that stayed ÷ the same lender-held total.
    • Rank badges and Biggest moves rank year-moves (one sender, one receiver, one calendar year) by medallions; Smooth ranks the trailing 12 months against the same all-time list.
    • "Since 2000" pools the share: total moved ÷ sum of the sender's start-of-year books.
    • Arrow width grows with the square root of the flow, so small flows stay visible. Read exact counts in the inspector.
    • All lenders: every family that moved 50 or more medallions over 2000 to 2025; the rest sit in "Other lenders".

    Source: NY DOS UCC filings via Lexis. Holders and moves from stage 251 (holder of record, latest-loan rule); networks from stage 255 (holder_network.json, holder_network_full.json); page from stage 257.
